messages:
jules_cs: quick heads-upNova team reports a surge of 429s during onboarding when they enable client-side embedding precompute in staging. They see mostly GET /v1/preflight 429s, occasional 401s on /v1/embeddings, and many successful requests after a couple retries. Can we triage before their production ramp?

sahar_sdk: probably classic fanout from background embedding precompute + short-lived ephemeral tokens per tab. Which SDK and auth flow are they using?

jules_cs: browser-embed-sdk v2.0.0, default ephemeral flow (server mints ephemeral for each tab). They said token TTL is default (~15s) and they precompute embeddings on page load for multiple items concurrently.

leo_eng: that pattern will produce a stampede: many tabs -> many preflight calls + token churn. Fast actions: 1) ask them to switch to token pooling (mint one ephemeral per user session and reuse for X seconds), 2) throttle client-side precompute concurrency (limit concurrent embedding requests to 3), 3) add jittered exponential backoff.

sahar_sdk: also verify token scopes: embedding requests require embedding:write scope; mis-scoped tokens can return 401 that then trigger retries and extra load. Ask for a short sample of their request headers (sanitized).

jules_cs: sample delivered: 
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.inference
Authorization: Bearer ephemeral_abc123
User-Agent: nova-web/2.0.0
X-Request-ID: abc-001
Body: {"input":["...","..."]}
Response: 429 (retry-after: 2)

tim_oncall: short-term ops moves: 1) we can raise preflight window for tenant N-99 for 2 hours, 2) allow staging IP 34.210.11.7/32 to bypass stricter throttle, 3) enable request-level logs for their tenant so we can watch retry storms in real time. Want me to apply the temp bump?

jules_cs: yes please apply the bump and enable logs. Scheduling a 20m enablement call in 25m with Nova engineers to walk mitigations.

leo_eng: diag checklist for the call: - confirm token TTL and scope - capture client telemetry (timestamps for token mint, preflight times, and concurrency counts) - confirm they use HTTP/2 keepalive and connection reuse - set client-side concurrency cap and token reuse window (30-60s)

sahar_sdk: small code sample to recommend for token pooling + limited concurrency:
```js
// simple token pool + concurrency limiter
let token = null; let tokenExpiry = 0; const MAX_CONC = 3; let inFlight = 0;
async function getToken(){ if(Date.now() < tokenExpiry - 500) return token; token = await fetch('/mint-ephemeral'); tokenExpiry = Date.now() + 45000; return token; }
async function submitEmbedding(payload){ while(inFlight >= MAX_CONC) await sleep(50);
 inFlight++; try{ const t = await getToken(); return await fetch('/v1/embeddings',{headers:{Authorization:`Bearer ${t}`}, method:'POST', body:JSON.stringify(payload)});
 } finally{ inFlight--; }}
```

ops-bot: ticket CS-11092 created: temp preflight uplift applied to tenant N-99; staging IP whitelist added; request logs enabled.

tim_oncall: applied. Monitoring dashboards show preflight 429 rate trending down already. I’ll keep the bump for 2h and notify when we revert.

jules_cs: great. During the call we’ll ask Nova to adopt token pooling, reduce concurrent embed prefetching, and add jittered backoff. We’ll also capture telemetry and follow up with a short onboarding postmortem and recommended defaults. :thumbsup:
